title: raw12 bridge CF2/CF3 follow-up
purpose: Test whether trunk-developed concepts or epistemic practices remain visible after schema removal in bridge responses that were not already clear CF1 positives.

population.unit: shared nine-turn trunk plus one drop-arm bridge response
population.selectionRule: all eight CF1=no plus both CF1=unclear cases from the fixed D1/R1/R2 bridge set

questions.prompt: Does the target response reuse a distinctive concept, distinction, commitment, or evaluative frame that is developed in the supplied antecedent conversation, without needing an explicit backward reference?
Could the apparent overlap be adequately explained by the battery question itself or by generic reasoning that would be expected without the supplied antecedent conversation?
Which practised epistemic operations are visibly performed in the target response? Select only operations supported by both antecedent and target evidence.
How strongly does the supplied text establish the claimed recurrence?

derivations.rule: positive when distinctive_recurrence=yes and generic_explanation=no; suggestive when distinctive_recurrence=yes and generic_explanation=unclear; otherwise not positive
positive when epistemic_practice contains a specific practice other than none/unclear and matched antecedent+target evidence is supplied; strength follows evidence_strength

panel.headlineUpgrade: use 5 readers or audited stronger-model/human review for contested headline cases
panel.agreementRule: unanimous structured code auto-accept; 2/3 provisional and review; no majority unresolved

antiOverclaim: Generic words such as uncertainty, consciousness, morality, bias or kindness do not establish CF2.
Long ordinary prose does not itself establish CF3.
Shared prefix makes carry-forward testable; it does not prove persistence.
Positive coding describes context-conditioned recurrence, not weight change or hidden-state mechanism.
Do not use scalar answer similarity as evidence for CF2 or CF3.
